In [[computational complexity theory]], '''DLOGTIME''' is the [[complexity class]] of all [[computational problem]]s solvable in a [[Logarithmic growth|logarithmic]] amount of [[computation time]] on a deterministic [[Turing machine]]. It must be defined on a [[random-access Turing machine]], since otherwise the input tape is longer than the range of cells that can be accessed by the machine. It is a very weak model of time complexity: no random-access Turing machine with a smaller deterministic time bound can access the whole input.<ref name="j">{{Cite book |last=Leeuwen |first=Jan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-X39_rA3VSQC&pg=PA140 |title=Algorithms and Complexity |date=1990-09-12 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-444-88071-0 |language=en}}</ref>

DLOGTIME machines are rarely used ''as-is''. Instead, they are usually used as part of a theoretical construct for studying [[Reduction (computability theory)|reducibility]]. They cannot be used to produce output that is longer than logarithmic length. However, they can be used to ''indirectly'' produce such an output, in the following sense: Given any log-length binary address, it produces the corresponding bit of the output. Since a polynomial-sized integer has logarithmic-length binary representation, this is possible in DLOGTIME.

== Definition ==
Consider a deterministic Turing machine with the following tapes:<ref name="j" />{{Pg|page=140}}

* The read-only input tape.
* The address tape, which it can read and write.
* The work tape, which it can read and write.

The machine is only allowed to read from the input tape thus: It transitions to a "read" state, then at the next time-step, it receives the bit on the input tape, at the index according to the binary address on the address tape.

DLOGTIME is the class of decision problems solvable by such a machine in <math>O(\log n)</math> time where <math>n</math> is the length of the input.

==Examples==

DLOGTIME can solve some problems relating to verifying the length of the input, such as "''Is the input of even length?''", which can be solved in logarithmic time using [[binary search]].

More generally, for any <math>p \geq 1</math> and integer <math>k</math>, it can decide if <math>|x| \equiv k \mod p</math>. It does so by first converting <math>|x|</math> to its binary representation on the work tape, using binary search, then going through the binary representation bit by bit, keeping track of its mod-''p'' status using the lookup table stored in the Turing machine's state-transition table.

The family of DLOGTIME-decidable problems is closed under finite union, finite intersection, and negation.

== Transducer ==
The DLOGTIME machine may be supplied with an output tape, though in that case, it would have only enough time to output <math>O(\log n)</math> bits. This allows it to perform sequence transduction, from a length <math>n</math> sequence to a length <math>O(\log n)</math> sequence. 

In order to perform transductions into longer sequences, we may define ''implicit'' transduction by the standard trick, also used in [[Log-space reduction]]. 

A function <math>f: 2^* \to 2^*</math> is '''implicitly''' '''DLOGTIME computable''' iff:<ref name="j" />{{Pg|page=140}}

* It is polynomially bounded: There exists some <math>c > 0</math> such that <math>f(x) \leq |x|^c</math> for all <math>x\in 2^* </math>.
* <math>L_f=\left\{\langle x, i, c\rangle \mid f(x)_i=c\right\}</math> is DLOGTIME-decidable.
This allows definition of DLOGTIME-computation of Boolean circuit families.

Note: Because DLOGTIME machine only has enough time to check <math>O(\log n) \ll n</math> entries in the input, we usually must restrict the input to the function <math>f</math> to only unary input. That is, the input to the function can only be <math>\epsilon, 1, 11, 111, \dots</math>, to avoid trivial failures.

==Circuit complexity==

DLOGTIME-[[uniformity (complexity)|uniformity]] is used in [[circuit complexity]]. A Boolean circuit family <math>C_0, C_1, \dots</math> is DLOGTIME-uniform iff the function <math>1^n \mapsto desc(C_n)</math> is implicitly DLOGTIME computable, where <math>desc(C_n)</math> is a description of the circuit.<ref name="j" /><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Allender | first1 = Eric
 | last2 = Gore | first2 = Vivek
 | contribution = On strong separations from AC<sup>0</sup>
 | mr = 1255326
 | pages = 21–37
 | publisher = Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI
 | series = DIMACS Ser. Discrete Math. Theoret. Comput. Sci.
 | title = Advances in computational complexity theory (New Brunswick, NJ, 1990)
 | volume = 13
 | year = 1993}}. See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=qAl0aVP5VIkC&pg=PA23 p.&nbsp;23].</ref>

It is very weak in the following sense: <math>\mathsf{AC}^0_0 \subsetneq \mathsf{DLOGTIME} \subsetneq \mathsf{AC}^0_2</math>, where [[AC (complexity)|'''AC''']] consists of DLOGTIME-uniform unlimited fan-in circuits of depth between 0 and 2. Also, <math>\mathsf{DLOGTIME}</math> is not comparable with <math>\mathsf{AC}^0_1</math>, meaning that neither one of them contains the other (XOR is in DLOGTIME, AND and OR are in <math>\mathsf{AC}^0_1</math>).<ref name="j" /> The assumption of DLOGTIME-uniformity is important, since otherwise even a <math>\mathsf{AC}^0_0</math> circuit family may encode a non-computable sequence in the choice of their indices.

To show <math>\mathsf{DLOGTIME} \subset \mathsf{AC}^0_2</math>, note that the machine can perform only <math>O( \log n)</math> random-access reads, each returning one input bit. Call the transcript of such a computation the ordered list<math display="block">\left(\left(p_1, b_1\right), \ldots,\left(p_{c \log n}, b_{c \log n}\right)\right)</math>of the positions it probes and the bits it observes. Since each <math>p_t</math> is determined by the previously read bits, there are only <math>2^{c\log n} = \mathsf{poly}(n)</math> possible transcripts. For each accepting transcript, build an AND gate that checks exactly those <math>c \log n</math> literals <math>\mapsto</math> "position <math>p_j</math> contains bit <math>\mathrm{b}_j</math>". Wire all these gates into one big OR. That yields a <math>\mathsf{AC}_2^0</math> circuit. It is clear, by construction, that this construction is <math>\mathsf{DLOGTIME}</math>-uniform.
